title: Fabrication of a Dipole-assisted Solid Phase Extraction Microchip for Trace Metal Analysis in Water Samples
protocol: Draw the network pattern of the chip using CAD software according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Mount a PMMA sheet on the working table of the laser micromachining system.
Focus the laser source on the surface of the PMMA sheet.
Select Print in the CAD software.
Set Power, Speed, and Pen Mode as 45% (4.5 W), 13% (99.06 mm sec−1), and VECT through the control panel of the micromachining system.
Print the drawn pattern.
Machine the PMMA sheet according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Drill three 1/16-inch diameter access holes on the bottom plate for a sample inlet, a buffer inlet, and an eluent inlet.
Drill one 1/16-inch diameter access hole on the cover plate for a confluent outlet.
Immerse the machined plates into 1 L of 0.1% (w/v) sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) solution in a 1-L beaker with agitation via an ultrasonic oscillator for 10 min.
Replace the SDS solution with deionized water and agitate via an ultrasonic oscillator for 10 min.
Immerse the machined plates in fresh deionized water with agitation via an ultrasonic oscillator for 10 min.
Dry each cleaned plate with a gentle stream of nitrogen for 2 min.
Align the two machined plates with the naked eye.
Sandwich the two plates between two glass boards using binder clips.
Bond the two plates under compression at 105 °C for 30 min.
Cool the sandwich to ambient temperature.
Remove the binder clips and glass boards.
Insert 1/16-inch outer diameter poly(etheretherketone) (PEEK) tubes into the access holes.
Secure the conduits with a two-component epoxy-based adhesive.
Dry the adhesive at ambient temperature for 12 hr.
Deliver a saturated sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution at a flow rate of 100 µl min-1 via a peristaltic pump into the microchip for 12 hr (72 ml total delivered volume).
Remove the residual solution and rinse the channel interior with D. I. H2O at a flow rate of 100 µl min-1 via a peristaltic pump for 30 min (3 ml total delivered volume).
Remove the residual D. I. H2O.
Deliver a 0.5% (v/v) nitric acid (HNO3) solution into the microchip at a flow rate of 100 µl min-1 via peristaltic pump for 30 min (3 ml total delivered volume).
Remove the residual solution and deliver a 50% (w/v) acrylamide solution into the microchip in the dark at a flow rate of 100 µl min-1 via peristaltic pump for 8 hr (48 ml total delivered volume).
Remove the residual solution.
Rinse the channel interior with D. I. H2O at a flow rate of 100 µl min-1 via a peristaltic pump for 30 min (3 ml total delivered volume).
Pump air to remove residual DI H2O from the microchip using a peristaltic pump.
Cover the microchip with an in-house-built photomask that exposes the desired region of the extraction channel to light.
Flush the inhibitor removal SPE cartridge with ethanol, amounting to at least three cartridge-volumes.
Flush the cartridge with 1,1'-dichloroethene, amounting to at least three cartridge-volumes prior to use.
Pass 1 ml of 1,1'-dichloroethene through the treated cartridge and collect the fraction in a sample vial wrapped in aluminum foil.
Add 491 μl of 1,1'-dichloroethene into a solution containing 12 mg AIBN, 3.18 ml ethanol, and 1.65 ml hexanes in a 100-ml glass bottle.
Fill the chip channel with the Cl-containing SPE formation solution (approximately 200 μl) by syringe injection.
Expose the microchip to ultraviolet (UV365) irradiation for 10 minutes, with a maximum emission wavelength of 365 nm and light intensity of ~2.65 mW cm-2.
Note: An appropriate exhaust system is recommended due to ozone production during UV irradiation.
Replace the residual solution with a fresh Cl-containing SPE formation solution by syringe injection.
Expose the microchip to UV365 irradiation for 10 min (light intensity ~2.65 mW cm-2).
Repeat Step 1.2.9 18 times.
Rinse the channel interior with ethanol at flow rate of 100 µl/min via peristaltic pump for 30 min.
Remove the residual solution with peristaltic pump after rinsing.
Store the fabricated microchip in a zippered bag for subsequent use.
Cut a PMMA sheet into substrates by laser micromachining system.
Immerse the PMMA substrates in 40 ml saturated NaOH solution and agitate via rocking shaker for 12 hr.
Remove residual NaOH solution and rinse with DI H2O.
Immerse substrates in 40 ml DI H2O and agitate via rocking shaker for 30 min.
Remove residual DI H2O.
Immerse substrates in 40 ml of 0.5% (v/v) HNO3 solution and agitate via rocking shaker for 30 min.
Remove residual HNO3 solution.
Immerse the PMMA substrates in a 40 ml of 50% (w/v) acrylamide solution and agitate in the dark for 8 hr.
Rinse PMMA substrates with 40 ml D.I. H2O.
Agitate the PMMA substrates with D.I. H2O on a rocking shaker for 30 min.
Dry each PMMA substrate with a gentle stream of nitrogen for 2 min.
Flush the inhibitor removal SPE cartridge with ethanol amounting to at least three cartridge-volumes.
Flush the cartridge with 1,1'-dichloroethene amounting to at least three cartridge-volumes prior to use.
Pass 6 ml of 1,1'-dichloroethene through the treated cartridge and collect in a sample vial wrapped in aluminum foil.
Add 4.91 ml 1,1'-dichloroethene into a solution containing 120 mg AIBN, 31.8 ml ethanol, and 16.5 ml hexanes in a 100-ml glass bottle.
Apply 2 ml of the Cl-containing SPE formation solution onto the surfaces of the PMMA substrates.
Expose the substrates to UV365 irradiation for 10 min (light intensity ~2.65 mW cm-2).
Replace residual solution with 2 ml of fresh Cl-containing SPE formation solution.
Expose the substrates to UV365 irradiation for another 10 min (light intensity ~2.65 mW cm-2).
Repeat Step 2.1.12 18 times.
Rinse PMMA substrates with 40 ml ethanol in a 50-ml conical tube.
Remove the residual solution from PMMA substrates.
Rinse the PMMA substrates with 40 ml D.I. H2O.
Dry each PMMA substrate with a gentle stream of nitrogen for 2 min.
Drop 5 μl D.I. H2O onto the PMMA substrates.
Determine the contact angle using a contact angle meter according to manufacturer's protocol.
Grind 8 g of PMMA beads into powders via mortar and pestle.
Immerse the PMMA powders in 40 ml saturated NaOH solution in a 50-ml conical tube.
Agitate the resulting mixtures via a rocking shaker for 12 hr.
Remove the residual solution using a digital pipette with 5-ml tips.
Rinse the PMMA powders with 40 ml D.I. H2O.
Immerse the PMMA powders in 40 ml D.I. H2O and agitate via a rocking shaker for 30 min.
Remove the residual D.I. H2O.
Immerse the PMMA powders in 40 ml of 0.5% (v/v) HNO3 solution and agitate via a rocking shaker for 30 min.
Remove the residual solution.
Immerse the PMMA powders in 40 ml of 50% (w/v) acrylamide solution and agitate in the dark for 8 hr.
Remove the residual solution.
Rinse the PMMA powders with 40 ml D.I. H2O.
Immerse PMMA powders in 40 ml of D. I. H2O.
Agitate the mixture via a rocking shaker for 30 min.
Remove residual D. I. H2O from the PMMA powders.
Bake the PMMA powders at 60 °C for 8 hr.
Flush the inhibitor removal SPE cartridge with ethanol amounting to at least three cartridge-volumes.
Flush the cartridge with 1,1'-dichloroethene amounting to at least three cartridge-volumes prior to use.
Pass 16 ml of 1,1'-dichloroethene through the treated cartridge and collect in a sample vial wrapped in aluminum foil.
Add 14.73 ml of 1,1'-dichloroethene into the solution containing 360 mg AIBN, 95.4 ml ethanol, and 49.5 ml hexanes in a 250-ml glass bottle.
Mix PMMA powders with 6 ml of Cl-containing SPE formation solution in a 50-ml conical tube.
Transfer 1 ml of the mixture from the conical tube into six wells of a 24-well tissue culture plate.
Cover the tissue culture plate with a PMMA board.
Expose the tissue culture plate to UV365 irradiation for 10 min (light intensity ~2.65 mW cm-2).
Replace residual solution in each well with 1 ml of fresh Cl-containing SPE formation solution.
Expose the tissue culture plate to UV365 irradiation for 10 min again (light intensity ~2.65 mW cm-2).
Repeat step of replacing residual solution and exposing to UV365 irradiation 18 times.
Rinse PMMA powders in each well with 1 ml ethanol.
Remove residual ethanol from the wells.
Rinse PMMA powders in each well with 1 ml deionized water.
Remove residual deionized water from the wells.
Bake PMMA powders at 60 °C for 8 hours.
Compress dried PMMA powders (1 g) to a pellet using a hydraulic press machine.
Measure Cl signal by LA-ICP-MS system, selecting m/z 35 as an indicator for C-Cl moieties.
Use a 193-nm laser with energy settings of 75%, fluence of 8.85 J/cm², spot size of 100 μm, and repetition rate of 5 Hz.
Perform at least seven repeated measurements for each result.
Take Raman spectra by Raman spectrometer using a 780-nm laser line with maximum power of 100 mW.
Investigate the attachment of C-Cl moieties to PMMA in the region from 550 to 900 cm⁻¹.
Immerse 0.5 g PMMA powders in 5 ml of 20% (w/v) manganese nitrate tetrahydrate solution.
Mix the resulting mixture with 5 ml of 40 mM maleate buffer solution equally.
Adjust the pH of the resulting mixtures to 8 using a pure HNO3 solution.
Agitate the mixtures via a rocking shaker for 1 hour.
Remove the residual solution.
Bake the PMMA powders at 60 °C for 8 hours.
Store the powders in a 15-ml conical tube wrapped in aluminum foil.
